findings.message:
[P1] Invalidate the pending defaults debounce on target changes

If an edit schedules the 500 ms save and the operator changes `baseSelect` before it fires, `clearDefaultsSaveQueue()` only resets the flag; the pending callback still enters this new branch and queues a save for the new target. The subsequent load can then POST freshly loaded or fallback values to the newly selected gateway; cancel or invalidate the pending debounce when the target changes.

static/admin.js:10481-10483

[P2] Reconcile filtered key views after concurrent edits

When an expiry PATCH response arrives after another input changed during the request, `inputsUnchanged` is false and this rerender is skipped. `updateKeyStatus()` only changes the existing row's state and text, so the key remains in the old Active/Expired tab and an extended key gets no new expiry timer until another reload or queued save.

static/admin.js:7363-7363

[P3] Give live expired rows a warning accent

The new status refresh writes `data-state="expired"`, but `static/style.css` still defines accents only for `active`, `warning`, and `revoked`; rows that expire while open or are edited to an expired date therefore fall back to the muted accent instead of the warning accent. Use the warning state or add an expired-row rule.

static/admin.js:7145-7148

summary: The patch retains a cross-target defaults-save race and incomplete live key rendering.

evidence: The pending debounced defaults save is not invalidated by the target-change handler, so the candidate can still queue a POST for the newly selected gateway.
The candidate leaves static/style.css without an expired-row accent rule while static/admin.js assigns data-state="expired".

The added JavaScript tests only regex-match source text and do not exercise delayed/reload saves, revoke cancellation, expired unrevoke behavior, or expired-key rendering; the route list also omits the revoke and unrevoke endpoints.
